setup: VoiceStampSpikeTests on the 50 real-voice recordings. Every vocabulary term spoken in 2 or more recordings (18 terms, 39 occurrences) gives one-shot stamps: the occurrence's stretch of Parakeet CTC 110M token posteriors, located by the CTC keyword spotter. Each stamp is matched against the other 49 recordings with subsequence DTW (frame cost -log of the posterior dot product). Word Boost misses come from a production Express + Word Boost run on the same recordings. Scored with voice_stamp_spike.py.
decision_rule: Fixed before the run: go if, at a threshold with at most 1% false alarms over (stamp, recording) pairs without the term, stamps find and place at least half of the occurrences Express + Word Boost misses.
verdict: Go for a prototype, not for shipping. With the blank token removed, stamps meet the rule (5 of 9 Word Boost misses at 1% pair false alarms) and still recover 5 at 0.1 false alarms per recording. With the blank kept they find nothing.
caveats: Of the 5 recovered misses, 4 are product terms (Orttaai twice, Xcode, appcast); among names only Folasade in one recording, 1 of the 5 missed names (Folasade x2, Ngozi, Temitope, Yemisi).
One-shot stamps cut from running speech; the planned feature records a name deliberately three times, which should give cleaner stamps but is untested.
The worst false alarms come from very short stamps (2 frames, a soft trailing 'Folasade'); a minimum stamp length would remove several.
Where a term sits in a recording comes from the CTC spotter, which knows the spelling; for badly modelled names that placement is itself uncertain.
next_step: Record three deliberate takes of each name, rerun this harness with them as stamps, and require a minimum stamp length and Word Boost's acoustic check before any replacement.
